svg.title: A client says, "My home pregnancy test was positive, so I know I'm pregnant." Why does the nurse explain that a positive test is only a probable sign?
svg.desc: A pregnancy test measures hCG , and hCG can be raised by other things, such as a hydatidiform mole or some tumors, so the result is probable, not positive. The provider may confirm it with a serum hCG and later with ultrasound, fetal heart tones or fetal movement felt by the examiner.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Physiologic & Psychological
Changes of Pregnancy
Read the situation
A client says, "My home pregnancy test was
positive, so I know I'm pregnant." Why
does the nurse explain that a positive
test is only a probable sign?
What fits here
The test detects hCG, which can be raised
by conditions other than pregnancy
Why it fits
A pregnancy test measures hCG , and hCG
can be raised by other things, such as a
hydatidiform mole or some tumors, so the
result is probable, not positive. The
provider may confirm it with a serum hCG
and later with ultrasound, fetal heart
tones or fetal movement felt by the
examiner.
